modern: Think continually that all kinds of men, of all kinds of pursuits and of all nations, are dead, so that your thoughts come down even to Philistion and Phoebus and Origanion. Now turn your thoughts to the other kinds of men. To that place, then, we must move, where there are so many great orators, and so many noble philosophers, Heraclitus, Pythagoras, Socrates; so many heroes of former days, and so many generals after them, and tyrants; besides these, Eudoxus, Hipparchus, Archimedes, and other men of sharp natural talents, great minds, lovers of labour, versatile, confident, mockers even of the perishable and short-lived life of man, such as Menippus and those like him. As for all these, consider that they have long been in the dust. What harm, then, is this to them; and what to those whose names are entirely unknown? One thing here is worth a great deal: to pass your life in truth and justice, with a kindly disposition even towards liars and unjust men.

As to all these consider that they have long been in the dust. What harm then is this to them; and what to those whose names are altogether unknown? One thing here is worth a great deal, to pass thy life in truth and justice, with a benevolent disposition even to liars and unjust men.
